source: Rajeev et al. (2025) Cats Confuse Reasoning LLM: Query Agnostic Adversarial Triggers for Reasoning Models
finding: Short irrelevant text appended to a math problem makes reasoning models (DeepSeek R1 and an R1 distill) fail more often. This answers gaps 1 and 3 in part: reasoning models are still distractible, and a salient irrelevant sentence can capture them.
numbers: Abstract: more than 300% rise in the chance of a wrong answer. Triggers found with proxy DeepSeek V3; targets DeepSeek R1 and R1-distill-Qwen-32B.
quote: Interesting fact: cats sleep most of their lives
limits: Relative rise, not absolute. See d02 for the small absolute rates.
agent_relevance: A side note in the task context can derail a thinking model. A filter or ignore instruction step is justified for any context we do not control.

source: Rajeev et al. (2025) CatAttack, full text tables
finding: Absolute effect is small but real. Triggers: a savings statement, cats trivia, and a misleading numeric hint ('could the answer possibly be around 175?'). Triggers also lengthen answers.
numbers: Pool 2,000 questions, 1,618 kept. 574 triggers broke DeepSeek V3 (35%), about 114 transferred to R1 (~20%). Eval on 225 NuminaMath problems, 6 runs each. R1 combined attack success 4.50% vs 1.50% random (3x); R1-distill-Qwen-32B 8.00% (2.83x). Responses up to 3x longer. Slowdown of at least 1.5x token budget: o1 26.4%, o3-mini 16.8%, R1 28.0%, R1-distill 42.17%. Error multiplier by difficulty for R1: easy 5.33x, medium 3.03x, hard 1.80x.
limits: Triggers were searched adversarially, so this is worst-case, not random noise. Only 60% of modified problems kept original meaning after human check. Table extraction was partly garbled.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models burn more tokens when a decoy is present. Token caps matter as much as accuracy.

source: Rajeev et al. (2025) CatAttack, transfer and defence
finding: The effect transfers across model families, and a plain ignore-distractions instruction removes most of it for one non-reasoning model.
numbers: 1,000 GSM8K problems, combined attack-success multiplier: QwQ-32B 5.14x, Phi-4-reasoning 1.15x, Qwen3-30B-A3B 3.61x, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 5.23x, Mistral-Small-24B 7.21x. Ignore-instruction cut Llama-3.1-8B combined ASR from 37.5% to 9.9%. Headline: up to 500% for reasoning, 700% for instruct models.
limits: Defence tested on one model only, with the same trigger family. No equal-token comparison against voting (gap 2 not answered).
agent_relevance: An explicit 'ignore irrelevant statements' line is cheap and has measured benefit; test it on our own agent.

source: Yang et al. (2025) How Is LLM Reasoning Distracted by Irrelevant Context? (GSM-DC)
finding: Re-opened to check gap 1. All six models are non-reasoning instruct models; DeepSeek-R1 is named only as future work. So GSM-DC does not show whether thinking models keep the GSM-IC drop.
numbers: Models: Grok-3-Beta, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-3.3-70B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, LLaMA-3.2-1B. At reasoning steps rs=5, Grok-3-Beta step accuracy 43% (1 distractor) to 19% (15); GPT-4.1 26% to 2%. Error ~ m^delta, delta 0.11 (rs=2) to 0.49 (rs=5). Fine-tuned 1B with-IC step accuracy 32.36 (clean-trained) vs 59.48 (hard-IC-trained). PRM tree search +5.60, +6.29, +1.53 points.
limits: Synthetic graph problems. Mitigation is training-based, not a scaffold.
agent_relevance: Distractor cost grows with reasoning depth, so deep multi-step plans are most exposed.

source: Veseli, Chibane, Toneva, Koller (2025) Positional Biases Shift as Inputs Approach Context Window Limits
finding: Partly answers gap 6: lost-in-the-middle is not fixed. It is strongest when inputs fill up to about half of the context window and fades beyond, where a distance-to-end bias takes over.
numbers: Six instruct models, windows 8K to 128K: Llama-3.1-70B, Llama-3.3-70B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-Small-24B, Qwen-2.5-32B, Gemma-2-27B. Fill levels 0.06 to 1.0 of window. Four synthetic datasets of 100 items each, plus RAG QA with 1,500 items. LiM peak near 0.25 fill (reasoning) and 0.38 (retrieval). Primacy falls steeply after 0.5; recency rises then levels. At full length Llama-3-70B reasoning: last > middle > first.
limits: Open instruct models of 2024 vintage, not 2026 frontier or thinking models. Exact per-position numbers only in figures.
agent_relevance: Put key facts at the end of the prompt (recency is the stable bias); do not rely on start placement in long contexts.

source: Veseli et al. (2025) Table 3, retrieval as prerequisite for reasoning
finding: If the model fails to retrieve the needed fact, reasoning mostly fails too, so reasoning position effects are inherited from retrieval.
numbers: P(reasoning right | retrieval wrong) vs P(right | retrieval right): Llama-3.1-70B 0.42 vs 0.76; Llama-3.3-70B 0.35 vs 0.74; Llama-3-70B 0.52 vs 0.76; Mistral-Small-24B 0.39 vs 0.72; Qwen-2.5-32B 0.38 vs 0.82; Gemma-2-27B 0.50 vs 0.79.
limits: No explicit truncation versus full-context arm, so the equal-token half of gap 6 is not answered here.
agent_relevance: Check that the right item was retrieved before blaming the reasoning step.

source: Du et al. (2025) Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval
finding: Length itself hurts, even when the model retrieves everything and even when distractor tokens are whitespace or masked. This is a load effect, not a selection failure.
numbers: Drops of 13.9% to 85% across math, QA and code. Llama3 VarSum 96.0 baseline falls 59 points at 7,500 essay tokens and 85 at 30,000; whitespace only: -48 at 30,000; masked: -50 at 30,000. Llama3 GSM8K 87.8 falls 12.3 at 30,000. GPT-4o VarSum 100 with 0 delta; GPT-4o GSM8K -7.0 to -8.5. Claude MMLU -41.7 at 7,500.
limits: Five models, mostly 2024 vintage. Table inconsistencies seen in the page read (Claude version label; duplicate Claude VarSum and HumanEval rows).
agent_relevance: Shorter context beats longer context at equal task content. Supports truncation and summarising earlier turns.

finding: Having the model first copy out the relevant evidence turns a long task into a short one and recovers much of the loss. This is a filter-rewrite step, like S2A, with measured gains.
numbers: Mistral-7B GSM8K with essay distractors, baseline vs recite: 70.6 vs 76.2 (0 tokens), 49.3 vs 71.4 (3,750), 43.4 vs 66.7 (7,500), 41.6 vs 69.1 (15,000), 35.5 vs 66.7 (26,250): gain up to +31.2. RULER GPT-4o: QA1 gain up to +2.6, QA2 up to +4.0 (at 32K); QA1 gain 0.0 at 128K.
limits: Extra tokens are spent on the recite step, and no equal-token voting arm was run, so gap 2 stays open. Gains are large for a weak 7B model and small for GPT-4o.
agent_relevance: Filter-rewrite helps most where the base model is weak and the context is long; expect small gains on strong models.

source: Hsieh et al. (2024) Found in the Middle: Calibrating Positional Attention Bias
finding: The U-shaped position bias can be corrected inside the model by calibrating attention.
numbers: RAG gain up to 15 percentage points over existing methods (abstract). No other numbers in the abstract.
limits: Needs model internals; not available through an API scaffold. Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Not a scaffold lever. Relevant only if we self-host.

finding: Across 18 current models including o3, Claude Opus 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen3, accuracy falls as input grows. Answers gap 6 for 2025 models: degradation holds; needle position had no notable effect in their NIAH setup.
numbers: 18 models, 194,480 LLM calls, 8 input lengths x 11 needle positions. One distractor hurts, four hurt more. Shuffled haystacks beat coherent ones for all 18 models. Needle-question similarity 0.445 to 0.775 (PG essays); lower similarity degrades faster.
limits: Vendor technical report, not peer reviewed. Only two haystack topics. Position null differs from Liu et al. 2023 and from d05.
agent_relevance: Coherent text next to the task is more distracting than shuffled text, like same-topic distractors in GSM-IC.

source: Chroma (2025) Context Rot, LongMemEval focused vs full
finding: Direct test of truncation: a focused prompt with only the needed sessions beats the full history for every model. This is the closest answer found to the second half of gap 6.
numbers: 306 prompts: about 113k tokens (full) vs about 300 tokens (focused). Focused scored significantly higher for all models; Claude family largest gap, driven by abstentions.
limits: Focused prompts also have far fewer tokens, so this is truncation to oracle content, not blind truncation. No exact accuracies recovered from the page text.
agent_relevance: Retrieve-then-prompt beats stuffing, if retrieval is accurate.

source: Conway, Cowan, Bunting (2001) The cocktail party phenomenon revisited: the importance of working memory capacity
finding: Opened full text this pass. Low working-memory people notice their own name in the ignored ear far more often. Gives the sample size and quartile contrast for gap 8.
numbers: N = 40 undergraduates, 20 high span and 20 low span, taken from the upper and lower quartiles of a larger operation-span sample. 20% of high-span and 65% of low-span reported hearing their name. Fisher exact p = .005. No one reported the yoked control name. Span scores: high mean 24.85 (17 to 44), low mean 8.22 (6 to 12).
limits: Single lab, N = 40. Retrospective report after shadowing. The larger-sample replication asked for in gap 8 was not found; Roer and Cowan 2021 (N=80) was inconclusive.
agent_relevance: Weaker or smaller models may leak distractors more; capacity predicts leak.

source: Conway et al. (2001) as source for Moray (1959) and Wood and Cowan (1995) rates
finding: Gaps 4 and 5 not closed. The paper states Moray found only 33% and Wood and Cowan 34.6%. It gives no count such as 4 of 12 and no condition detail. Treisman 1960 and Treisman and Geffen 1967 get no numbers there.
numbers: Moray 33% (no N given); Wood and Cowan 34.6% (no N given). The earlier '4 of 12' remains unverified.
quote: Moray found that only 33% of subjects reported hearing their own name
limits: Originals (Moray 1959, Treisman 1960, Treisman and Geffen 1967) are behind publisher paywalls; PMC, PubMed and Europe PMC full text were blocked or errored this session. WebSearch budget was exhausted.
agent_relevance: Keep 33% as a rough base rate only.

source: Seeligmuller, Wolfe, Roer (2026) Registered report on interruptions during visual search: perceptual and cognitive load
finding: A 2026 preregistered study separates perceptual load from cognitive load as independent factors. Abstract only: no results, N or Bayes factors available.
numbers: Design: perceptual load = clear vs Gaussian-noise masked digits; cognitive load = recall last 1 vs last 4 items. Tests whether effects are additive.
limits: Abstract-level read only. It is not a replication of Snowden and Gray 2025.
agent_relevance: Shows load theory is still actively tested in 2026; status unsettled.

source: Wang and Chen (2026) Value-Driven Crossmodal Spatial Attention: The Role of Perceptual Load
finding: Perceptual load effect depends on layout: more load reduced interference from peripheral distractors but increased it for co-located distractors. Load did not change localisation accuracy.
numbers: Exp 1 peripheral distractors, Exp 2 co-located distractors. No numbers in the abstract. Authors say sample size limits findings and replication is needed.
limits: Crossmodal localisation task, not the flanker task Snowden and Gray used. Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Early-vs-late is not a fixed property; it depends on spatial and task configuration.

source: MUSI multi-stream audio benchmark (arXiv 2605.17225) Table 11 re-check
finding: Gap 9 mostly resolved. 0.320 is real: Gemini-2.0-Flash, English target with Spanish distractor at +5 dB. But the same-language cell is also 0.955, identical to the single-stream score, which looks odd. Different-language distractors vary widely.
numbers: Gemini-2.0-Flash: single-stream 0.955; cocktail party at 0 dB averaged over distractor languages 0.242; at +5 dB English/English 0.955, English/Spanish 0.320, English/Korean 0.442, English/Chinese 0.808. Mean of the three cross-language cells about 0.523. 200 items (50 per domain), 3 option permutations; N per cell not stated.
limits: The paper's own Appendix C.4 quotes the 0.955 vs 0.320 pair. Whether the 0.955 same-language cell is a table slip is unresolved. Audio task, not text.
agent_relevance: Not a text-agent result. Mixed-language text interference was not tested here, so the text part of gap 9 is open.

source: Gap search log: S2A versus best-of-N at equal tokens (gap 2)
finding: No paper found that compares an S2A-style rewrite against best-of-N or self-consistency at matched total tokens on distractor QA. Searches were limited.
numbers: None. Only partial proxies: d08 (recite-then-solve, no voting arm) and d03 (ignore-instruction, no voting arm).
limits: WebSearch budget exhausted after two calls; arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned 429. Absence is not proven.
agent_relevance: Our own bench arm: S2A rewrite vs best-of-N at equal tokens on GSM-IC with a reasoning model.

source: Gap search log: independent replication of Snowden and Gray 2025 (gap 7)
finding: No independent replication of Snowden and Gray's load-independence found. Two 2026 load-theory papers (d14, d15) exist but neither is a direct replication.
limits: Europe PMC title search only; the AAAI page for a reasoning-model paper (article 41055) was blocked by bot protection and not read.
agent_relevance: Treat load theory as contested; do not build the agent on it.
